reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates the exact mechanism and outcomes (low friction ~0.09, two-order wear reduction, Ag nanocrystal formation) in a (TiNbZr)75Ag25 alloy, but the hypothesis applies these findings to a chemically distinct CoCrFeNi matrix without direct evidence that the same tribochemical reactions and structural mediator will occur in this new system.
premises: Ag addition to a multi-component alloy can promote in-situ formation of an amorphous-crystalline nanocomposite tribolayer containing Ag nanocrystals during sliding in air.
Such a tribolayer can yield a very low friction coefficient (~0.09) in a ball-on-disk test.
The in-situ formed nanocomposite layer can reduce wear rate by two orders of magnitude compared to the undoped reference alloy.
The mechanism involves environmental oxygen reacting with the alloy, where Ag's positive enthalpy of mixing with other elements drives Ag nanocrystal nucleation.
